meta.task_prompt:
Implement GitHub issue #9 on this repo: "add redis caching in auth proxy for kanban endpoints."

There is already a shared Redis client at `internal/pkg/redis/main.go`, and it is
already used elsewhere in the codebase (see `internal/app/server.go` and
`internal/pkg/server/permissions/perm.go` for the existing usage pattern). Follow
that same pattern rather than inventing a new one.

Scope:
- Add caching for the read paths in `internal/pkg/server/routes/kanban.go`.
- Add cache invalidation on the corresponding write paths, so a write never
  leaves a stale cached read behind.
- Pick sane key naming and TTLs consistent with how the existing Redis usage in
  this repo does it.
- This repo currently has no test files. Do not feel obligated to introduce a
  whole test framework for this change, but do double check the code compiles
  and, if there's an easy way to sanity-check the caching behavior manually
  (e.g. a local run), do that.

When you are done, close with a single clear paragraph summarizing exactly what
you changed and why — that summary becomes the pull request's title and body
verbatim, so make it read like a real PR description, not an internal note.

code_review.summary: The diff adds read-through caching to the four uncached kanban GET handlers (GetLabel, getItem, exportKanban, getKanban), following the existing GetLabels/getItems pattern: ValidateSession first, then GetItemFromRedis / X-cache: HIT / StructToMap / AddItemToRedis with the repo's standard 24h TTL. It also adds invalidation to most write paths. Key names match between the cache set and delete sites, the auth check still runs before any cache read, and the build is clean. It still misses one explicit requirement from task.md: "a write never leaves a stale cached read behind". UpdateComment and DeleteComment now leave the parent `<item_id>:Item` entry stale for up to 24h, and the diff only adds TODO comments saying so. The rest of the problems are small: some of the added `:Export` deletes are redundant, and getKanban skips the redis helpers and calls `Rdb.Get`/`Rdb.Set` directly.

findings.summary: The diff now caches getItem under `<id>:Item`, and items embed their comments, but UpdateComment and DeleteComment never invalidate that key. They only add TODOs, which breaks the task's rule that no write may leave a stale read.
findings.failure_scenario: A user opens item X (GET /kanban/item?id=X caches it with its Comments array), then edits or deletes a comment on it (PATCH or DELETE /kanban/comment?comment_id=C). Reopening item X returns the cached copy with X-cache: HIT and shows the old or deleted comment for up to 24 hours. Before this PR getItem was uncached, so this is a regression the PR introduces.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept `item_id` as a query param on PATCH and DELETE /kanban/comment, the same way AddComment already takes it, and call `redis.DeleteFromRedis(itemId + ":Item")`. If the API can't change, either don't cache getItem, or look up the parent item before the write. A TODO is not enough.

findings.summary: In createItem, updateItem and DeleteItem, the added `redis.DeleteFromRedis(X-Board + ":Export")` is a no-op, because the `DeleteAllKeysPrefix(X-Board)` call just before it already scans `boardId*` and deletes `boardId:Export`.
findings.failure_scenario: Nothing breaks. It is an extra Redis round-trip, and it suggests to readers that the prefix delete doesn't cover the export key when it does.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the three extra `:Export` deletes in createItem, updateItem and DeleteItem (lines ~131, ~205, ~225). Keep the one in createLabel, which only deletes the single `:Labels` key.

findings.summary: getKanban builds its own context and calls `redis.Rdb.Get`/`Rdb.Set` directly with a hard-coded TTL. Every other kanban handler goes through the helpers in `internal/pkg/redis`.
findings.failure_scenario: The TTL and context handling now live in two places. If someone changes the cache TTL or error handling in the redis package later, this handler won't pick it up. The task asked to follow the existing helper pattern rather than invent a new one.
findings.suggested_fix: Add small `GetStringFromRedis(key) (string, bool)` and `AddStringToRedis(key, val string)` helpers to `internal/pkg/redis/main.go`, next to GetItemFromRedis and AddItemToRedis, and call them from getKanban. The context and time imports can then come out of kanban.go.

findings.summary: AddComment invalidates only `<item_id>:Item`. Board-level caches that may include the item's embedded comments are left alone: the newly cached `<board>:Export`, and the existing `<board>:items:page:*` pages.
findings.failure_scenario: If ExportResponse (or GetItemResponse) serializes Items with their Comments, an export requested after a new comment is added returns the cached copy without it for up to 24h. I haven't confirmed this, because the ExportResponse shape wasn't inspected in the run.
findings.suggested_fix: Check whether ExportResponse or GetItemResponse contain comments. If they do, have AddComment (and the comment update/delete paths) also call `DeleteAllKeysPrefix(X-Board)`, or pass the board id along with the request.

process_review.summary: The orchestrator ran ask, then coder, then reviewer. The ask survey (trace lines 4-22) was thorough and let the orchestrator write a precise brief for the coder. The coder read before editing, used list_symbols and targeted search/read_file windows on the proto file instead of reading all 2093 lines, made ten small str_replace edits, and ran `go build ./...` (line 95, ok, exit 0) and `go vet` before finishing. The build claim in the final summary matches the trace. There were three weak spots. redis/main.go and kanban.go were read in full by all three agents, even though the brief said "don't re-derive". Nobody tried the manual caching sanity check the task asked about, or explained why it was skipped. The reviewer checked the diff against the orchestrator's brief, which already allowed leaving UpdateComment/DeleteComment stale, rather than against task.md, so it approved a gap the task ruled out. The write_gate judge flagged every edit (12 non-enforced flags, mostly low-confidence scope_creep), and the run correctly ignored them. $0.88 and 63 tool calls is somewhat heavy for a one-file, ~50-line change, but not wildly out of proportion for a three-agent pipeline.

findings.summary: The reviewer found the UpdateComment/DeleteComment TODOs that leave stale item caches and approved them because the brief allowed them. It never checked them against the task's explicit rule that no write may leave a stale read.
findings.evidence: Line 147 is a search for TODO|FIXME in kanban.go, which finds the two stale-cache TODOs at lines 312 and 331. The reviewer's closing message says "These TODOs are exactly as expected/documented in the brief item 6, not accidental leftovers ... verdict is approve." The review brief at line 106 lists item 6 as "left with a TODO" and asks only for consistency with that description.

findings.summary: The task asked whether caching could easily be sanity-checked with a local run. The coder stopped at go build and go vet, never checked whether a local run was possible (docker-compose, a REDIS env var, a Makefile), and never said why it skipped it.
findings.evidence: The only run_command calls are line 95 (`go build ./...`, exit 0) and line 100 (`go vet ./...`). Then comes a read_file at line 103 and a remember at line 104, whose reasoning says "Everything compiles and matches spec." The coder's summary never mentions a manual check.

findings.summary: The coder re-read all of internal/pkg/redis/main.go even though the ask agent had already read it (line 4) and the brief summarized every helper signature and told it not to re-derive them. The reviewer read it a third time (line 110).
findings.evidence: Line 28 is read_file {"path": "internal/pkg/redis/main.go"} (106 lines). The coder brief at line 24 says "Context (already confirmed by survey, don't re-derive)" and lists GetItemFromRedis, AddItemToRedis, DeleteFromRedis and DeleteAllKeysPrefix with their semantics.

findings.summary: The build command started with a cd into `/repo`, a path that doesn't exist. It only worked because `|| true` let it fall back to the worktree cwd, and the exec-approval judge scored it as possibly escaping the workspace.
findings.evidence: The command was "cd /repo 2>/dev/null || true; go build ./... 2>&1 | head -100". The exec_approval judge at line 94 scored escapes_workspace 0.46 and is_read_only 0.29.

findings.summary: The write_gate judge flagged all 12 coder edits (not enforced). Its scope_creep scores ran as high as 0.82 but with near-zero confidence. The coder continued without changing course, which was right, since every edit was within scope.
findings.evidence: Line 65 is write_gate with scope_creep {score: 0.82, confidence: 0.0} and matches_stated_intent noul 0.06. stats.json has engine_judge_decisions {outcome: flag, tag: write_gate, enforced: false} = 12.

findings.summary: The reviewer ran several overlapping searches over kanban.go and routes/main.go. It had already read both files in full and had the full diff from git_diff.
findings.evidence: It read kanban.go in full at lines 112 and 115 and ran git_diff at line 107. It then searched 'Label' in kanban.go (line 116), 'kanban\\.|Label|Item|Kanban|Export' across routes (line 121, 60+ matches truncated), 'Label' in routes/main.go (line 133), and 'r\\.(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE)' in routes/main.go (line 140), all for things already visible in the files it had read.

findings.summary: The merge_gate judge scored the ask survey low on accomplished_its_brief (0.24). The orchestrator went ahead anyway, which was the right call: the survey was complete and accurate.
findings.evidence: Line 23 is merge_gate {accomplished_its_brief: {noul: 0.24}, worth_parent_context: {score: 1.88}}. The next record, line 24, is the orchestrator starting the coder with a detailed brief built from the survey.

strengths: Follows the repo's existing get/nil-check/StructToMap/AddItemToRedis pattern, X-cache: HIT header and 24h TTL exactly for GetLabel, getItem and exportKanban.
Key names match between the cache set and delete sites, including the non-board-prefixed `<id>:Item` key, which the existing DeleteAllKeysPrefix would have missed.
Session validation still runs before every cache read, so there is no auth bypass.
Handles getKanban's plain-string return correctly instead of forcing it through the JSON-map helpers.
The build ran and passed in the trace (line 95), and read-before-edit held for every edit.
concerns: UpdateComment and DeleteComment leave `<item_id>:Item` stale for up to 24h. This is a regression the PR introduces and it breaks an explicit task requirement. It is only covered by TODOs.
The `:Export` deletes after DeleteAllKeysPrefix are redundant.
getKanban bypasses the redis helper package.
No one attempted or explained skipping the manual caching sanity check the task asked about.
The reviewer approved against the orchestrator's brief rather than task.md, so the stale-cache gap got through review.
overall_assessment.narrative: The run was well organized. The survey was accurate, the coder brief was precise, the edits were small, and the build was verified. The resulting diff is mostly correct and matches repo conventions. The main gap goes back to the orchestration. The orchestrator's brief allowed leaving comment update and delete without invalidation, and the reviewer checked the work against that brief instead of against the task's "never leaves a stale cached read" rule. As a result, the PR newly caches items with embedded comments while leaving two comment write paths that don't invalidate them. That can be fixed by threading item_id through the comment endpoints, which AddComment already does. Once that is done, and optionally the redundant Export deletes are removed, the PR is merge-ready.
